mornings.title: KINDERGARTEN MORNINGS
mornings.eat_joke: If this is a copay, I want the sandwich in writing.

opener.text: We lived together then. Kindergarten mornings. I'd come home from work and you were still small enough to fit under my arm.

yes.text: Skylanders. Grandpa's room. Every other weekend.
I miss that time. I'm glad we had the time we had.
It's always been easy to talk to you. I'm proud of you.
Best son a dad could ask for. You've shown that.

no.text: That's alright. You were little. I remember enough for both of us.
Still proud. That's the whole sentence.

nerf.title: ONE-DAY WAR
nerf.eat_joke: Ammo's foam. Lunch is real. That's growth.

opener.text: Remember the Nerf war that lasted one day? Until Mom came home.

yes.text: The one that lasted until the door opened.

no.text: I remember the darts. Not the sequel.

deflect.text: Foam doesn't count as a war.

school.title: MILK CARTON
school.eat_joke: I packed this. That's the one assignment I finished.

opener.text: Remember I was at school a lot?

yes.text: You were there. Then you weren't. Then you were laughing.
I'd gone home to fetch something. Came back. You showed me a little man you'd made. I thought you were so clever.
After class the teacher wanted me alone. You stepped out. I said you'd made a really nice little man.
She had both hands on her head. THAT'S NOT WHAT THEY WERE SUPPOSED TO MAKE. LOOK. Everyone did the same milk-carton project. Except you.
I gave him a Nintendo. I've tried everything.
I couldn't stop laughing. Funny and uncomfortable. I knew myself in that.
I saw it wouldn't go well if it stayed like this. Still proud you only did what you liked. And how happy you were showing it.

no.text: I remember the little man. Not the meeting.
She had both hands on her head. Everyone made a milk carton. You made a person.
I laughed. It was uncomfortable. I was still proud.

sundays.title: EVERY SUNDAY
sundays.eat_joke: Last quiet meal before we jump. Chew like we mean it.

opener.text: I'm glad you've called every Sunday since we talked.
You understood more than I wanted you to. How much I miss you. How sad I am I wasn't who I wanted to be.
I tried everything. Work. Be a dad the right way. It still wasn't enough.
I'm sorry I failed at the most important thing I ever had. I didn't want you to notice. You read me like an open book.
From then: we talk every Sunday. You've kept it. It means more than you know.
I love you. I hope you know. I would never have left if I didn't have to.
One day I'll tell you more. I thought I'd made it so it couldn't happen. I was wrong. Rest of that story another day.
Still doesn't feel good. I'm sorry I failed you.

yes.text: Then we finish this together. I've got a feeling we'll get back together. All the time in the world.

no.text: I kept Sunday. That's the sentence I can say.
That's enough. I'm still proud. We finish this together.

deflect.text: Wind's loud. Let's not do the whole novel.

second.prompt: Maybe one day I make a game that makes us some money. Grandpa's house. Your old room. You the animals. Me the crops. You want that talk?

yes.text: Animals. You can have the crops.
Deal. Then we jump the hell down. Last push. So close I can taste it. Come on. Let's kick it, son.

no.text: Different dream. Same Sunday. Then we jump the hell down. Last push. Come on. Let's kick it, son.

deflect.text: Finish the game first. Then we argue about chickens.
Alright. Jump the hell down. Last push. Come on. Let's kick it, son.
